about: The routes of the 1838-39 Cherokee removal, as the National Park Service maps the congressionally designated Trail of Tears National Historic Trail.
source: National Park Service, National Trails Intermountain Region, Trail of Tears National Historic Trail, 2021-07-21. NPS DataStore reference 2238914.
licence: Public domain, 17 U.S.C. 105 (work of the US federal government). Originator, per the FGDC metadata and per every feature in the data: National Park Service, National Trails Intermountain Region, GIS. No third-party copyright holder, no partner or contractor with retained rights, no additional use constraints.
credit: The Trail of Tears Association appears in the MAPSOURCE field of 74 segments, as material the Park Service digitised from. It is credited here for that; it is not the author of any line.
scale_constraint: The source states: "This data set should not be displayed or used at scales that exceed 1:100,000." That is a bound on accuracy, not on rights. The route is drawn no finer than it, and the popup says so.
alignment_caveat: The Park Service notes that the designated alignment was identified before ground-verification and does not always coincide with the historic trace.
not_covered: The Trail of Tears National Historic Trail is the Cherokee removal. The Choctaw (1831-33), Muscogee (1836), Chickasaw (1837-38) and Seminole (1832-42) removals have no equivalent designated route dataset, and no line is drawn for them here.
simplified: Simplified at 0.002 degrees; measured maximum displacement 0.22 km.

routes.what: The river route: Tennessee, Ohio, Mississippi and Arkansas rivers.
The overland route through Tennessee, Kentucky, Illinois and Missouri.
The detachment under John A. Bell, which travelled separately.
Not a removal route. The roads along which people were taken from their homes to the stockades, before any march west began.
The detachment under John Benge, north through Alabama and Arkansas.
The overland legs of the river parties, where the water failed.
Not a removal route either. The roads along which the detachments broke up after arriving in Indian Territory, at the end of the march.
The detachment under Captain Gustavus Drane.
